Filters.Label: Filters
Filters.SearchPlaceholder: Type plain words to search by name. Add key:value filters to narrow the list.
Filters.ToggleCategory: Click to hide or show this category
Filters.NoMatch: No item in this category matches the filters.
Filters.SearchHint: Search by name. Narrow down with key:value (dashes instead of spaces, e.g. trait:cold-iron): trait:x — PF2e traits; rarity:x — common, uncommon, rare, unique; type:x — ammunition, armor, consumable, container, equipment, kit, shield, treasure, weapon; weapon-category:x (e.g. martial), weapon-group:x (e.g. sword, bow), armor-category:x (e.g. light), consumable-category:x (e.g. potion), ammunition-type:x (e.g. arrows). Separate several with spaces — items must match all of them. Use | for “or” within one word: weapon-group:axe|weapon-group:sword or, shorter, weapon-group:axe|sword (don't mix both forms in one word).

SyntaxGuide.Title: Syntax Guide
SyntaxGuide.AlertText: The search engine and its syntax are still in an early stage of development and may change in future versions.
SyntaxGuide.Credit: Syntax Guide inspired by Scryfall's search reference. Thank you, Scryfall team!

basics.Intro:
The search engine was built for Game Masters and players who need powerful ways to filter and categorize content. Whether you are looking for magic blades, arcane spells or anything else in the game world, it lets you find what you need right in Foundry VTT, without reaching for outside sources.

Besides searching by name, the engine offers a system of keys which, combined with the right values, narrow the results precisely and find exactly the items you want.

This Syntax Guide is split into sections for each category of content. Each one describes the keys available there and how to use them.

filters.Title: Key:value filters
filters.Text:
An expression in the form key:value filters the content. Values made of several words are written with dashes instead of spaces, e.g. trait:deadly-d12.

Unlike a plain name search, keys and their values must be typed in full or in a supported short form. For example, trait:mag will not find items with the magical trait.

The order of the keys doesn't matter — all filters apply at the same time. Any piece of text that isn't recognized as a key is treated as part of the item's name.

type.Title: Item types
type.Text:
The type:value key filters content by its type. This is the most general classification, based on the structure of the Pathfinder 2e system in Foundry VTT.

The same value can appear in different keys, but that doesn't mean they do the same thing. For example, type:consumable finds items of the Consumable type in Pathfinder 2e, while trait:consumable filters content that has the consumable trait, whatever its type.

Ammunition, for instance, can have the consumable trait even though its type is type:ammunition.

There is also a short form: ty:value. For example, ty:weapon works exactly like type:weapon.

Ex2.Text: Finds all consumables with the healing trait.

Ex3.Text: Finds all magical armor, using the short form of the key.

tags.Title: Key visualization
tags.Text:
When you press Space or Enter, or leave the search field, every key:value expression turns into a label in the Pathfinder 2e style.

Converted filters can still be edited or removed. To remove a filter, click the × next to its label. To edit it, double-click the label.

There are currently three kinds of labels:

  • Pathfinder 2e traits — shown in red. Example:
  • Rarity — shown in the rarity's own color; all four levels side by side:
  • Other keys — shown as plain labels when the value is valid, or with a dashed border when it isn't. Examples: (type:weapon) and (type:weapons).

logic.Intro: Beyond searching by name and filtering by key, the search engine supports logical operators. They let any player narrow a search down to exactly what they need right now, and work with both names and filters.

and.Title: AND Operator
and.Text: Every word and filter separated by a space must match the item. Anything that isn't a key:value filter is read as the item's name. The order of the name and filters doesn't matter.

Ex1.Text: Items with the agile and finesse traits

or.Title: OR Operator
or.Text:
The | sign searches for any one of several values. Put it between the values, with no spaces. You can list more than one value, but all of them must use the same key — trait:acid|trait:fire is valid, trait:acid|rarity:rare is not.

Short form: write the key only once; the values after the first, without a colon, reuse it. trait:acid|trait:fire works the same as trait:acid|fire. The group is one condition — other words still have to match too.

not.Title: NOT Operator
not.Text: The NOT operator excludes a specific name or filter from the search. Put ! before the key.

combine.Title: Combining operators
combine.Text: Operators can't be combined in one filter yet. This may arrive in the official 1.0 release.

traits.Intro:
Thanks to the hard work of Paizo and the creators of the Pathfinder 2e system for Foundry VTT, every item, spell and feat is described by one or more traits that define its properties and use. The game database contains hundreds of unique traits, each with its own function.

Because of their number and variety, they are not split into further categories. Instead, the search engine lets you look traits up directly by name — a single key is enough to find the entry you want.

trait.Title: Usage
trait.Text: To search with the official Pathfinder 2e property system, use the trait:value key or its short form, t:value. To see every trait that exists in the system, open All values below.

Ex2.Text: Items with the fire, cold or electricity trait, using the short form of the key

rarity.Intro: Every item and spell in Pathfinder has a rarity. Most items in the world of Pathfinder are classified as common, but some are harder to come by, and a few are one of a kind. To find such items, use the rarity:value key.

rarity.Title: Usage
rarity.Text: Items with no rarity listed are considered common. You can also use the short form of the key, r:value.

Ex2.Text: Rare shields, using the short form of the key

category.Title: Weapon category
category.Text: Use the weapon-category:value key, or its short form wct:value, to find weapons by their proficiency category.

group.Title: Weapon group
group.Text: Use the weapon-group:value key, or its short form wg:value, to find weapons by their group. Under the Pathfinder 2e rules, a weapon's group determines its critical specialization effect.

base.Title: Weapon base
base.Text: Use the weapon-base:value key, or its short form wb:value, to find weapons built on a specific base weapon.

range.Title: Weapon range
range.Text: Use the weapon-range:value key, or its short form wr:value, to set the range of the weapons you are looking for. Ranged weapons use their range increment in feet, e.g. weapon-range:60. Melee weapons use the value weapon-range:melee.
range.Note: In the future, I plan to add range filtering with the greater-than (>) and less-than (<) signs.

Ex2.Text: Weapons with a 60 ft. range increment

category.Title: Armor category
category.Text: Use the armor-category:value key, or its short form act:value, to find armor by its category. Light, medium and heavy armor use the short values light, medium and heavy, while barding uses the full values light-barding and heavy-barding. Clothing that grants no armor uses unarmored.

group.Title: Armor group
group.Text: Use the armor-group:value key, or its short form ag:value, to find armor by its group. Under the Pathfinder 2e rules, an armor's group determines its armor specialization effect.

base.Title: Armor base
base.Text: Use the armor-base:value key, or its short form ab:value, to find armor built on a specific base armor.

Ex1.Text: Every full plate, including magic ones

class.Title: Armor class
class.Text: Use the armor-class:value key, or its short form ac:value, to find armor by the AC bonus it grants. The value is the bonus as a number, e.g. armor-class:4 for a +4 bonus.

Ex2.Text: Armor with a +1 or +2 AC bonus

class.Title: Shield class
class.Text: Use the shield-class:value key, or its short form sc:value, to find shields by the AC bonus they grant. The value is the bonus as a number, e.g. shield-class:2 for a +2 bonus. Under the Pathfinder 2e rules, a shield grants this bonus only while it is raised.

Ex2.Text: Common shields with a +1 AC bonus

base.Title: Shield base
base.Text: Use the shield-base:value key, or its short form sb:value, to find shields built on a specific base shield.

Ex1.Text: Every steel shield, including magic ones

category.Title: Consumable category
category.Text: Use the consumable-category:value key, or its short form cct:value, to find consumables by their category, such as potions, elixirs, scrolls or talismans.

type.Title: Ammunition type
type.Text: Use the ammunition-type:value key, or its short form amt:value, to find ammunition by its type. Special ammunition without a chosen type, such as Beacon Shot, matches every type it can be made as. Parent types include their variants: rounds finds rounds for every firearm.

tradition.Title: Spell tradition
tradition.Text: Use the spell-tradition:value key, or its short form spt:value, to find spells on a specific tradition's spell list. Traditions are also item traits: trait:arcane finds items with the arcane trait, not arcane spells.

Ex2.Text: Spells on the arcane or occult list
